subject: chemistry
question_text: What is lanthanide contraction? What are its consequences?

verification.note: Chapter 2 is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.53-55), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. The 1+1+2 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. The book states the consequences as: 4d and 5d elements almost similar in size; 'they are not separated by the crystallization method'; Zr and Hf almost equal in size. The standard statement is that separation of the lanthanides is DIFFICULT because their sizes are nearly equal — crystallisation separates them poorly and ion-exchange methods are used — and the card says that; the book's flat 'not separated by crystallization' is recorded here rather than copied.

page_header: Classification of Elements – Periodic Properties · 4 marks

steps.label: The definition
lines: In the lanthanide series, the atomic and ionic
sizes decrease gradually as the atomic number
increases from lanthanum to lutetium.
This steady decrease in size is called the
lanthanide contraction.
steps.why: The definition is a trend, so it needs all three parts: which elements (the lanthanides), what changes (atomic and ionic size decrease), and along what (increasing atomic number).
common_mistakes: Writing that the size decreases suddenly. The decrease is small and steady across the fourteen elements.
Leaving out ionic size. The contraction shows in the ions as clearly as in the atoms.
steps.memory_tip: Fourteen elements, one slow shrink: La to Lu, each atom slightly smaller than the one before.
steps.margin_note: The words gradually and atomic number increases carry the definition.

steps.label: The cause
lines: Cause: the differentiating electrons enter the
4f orbitals, and 4f electrons screen the outer
electrons very poorly.
So with each added proton the outer shell
feels a greater effective nuclear charge and
is pulled inward.
steps.why: Across the series each new proton should be balanced by its new electron, but a 4f electron cancels very little of the extra pull — so the net pull on the outer shell keeps growing and the atom keeps shrinking.
common_mistakes: Writing poor shielding without naming the 4f orbitals. The orbital name is the marked word.
Saying the 4f electrons pull the outer electrons in. The nucleus pulls; the 4f electrons fail to screen it.
steps.memory_tip: The shape of a 4f orbital leaves the nucleus poorly covered, so every new proton is felt almost in full.
steps.margin_note: One phrase decides this mark: poor screening (shielding) by the 4f electrons.

steps.label: The consequences
lines: Consequences:
1. The 4d and 5d series elements have almost
the same size: zirconium and hafnium are
nearly equal in radius and occur together
in nature.
2. The lanthanides themselves are nearly
equal in size, so separating them is
difficult; crystallisation separates them
poorly and ion-exchange methods are used.

lines.text: Zr ≈ Hf in size, and the lanthanides are difficult to separate

steps.why: The contraction of the fourteen lanthanides cancels the size increase expected between the 4d and 5d rows, which is why Zr and Hf come out almost identical; inside the series, near-equal sizes mean near-equal properties and therefore difficult separations.
common_mistakes: Giving only one consequence for the two marks. Zr-Hf similarity and the difficult separation are both expected.
Writing that Zr and Hf are the same element. They are different elements of almost the same size.
steps.memory_tip: One shrink, two results: the row below matches the row above (Zr ≈ Hf), and the family members match each other (hard to separate).
steps.margin_note: Two numbered consequences for the two marks; the Zr–Hf pair is the example every scheme lists.

insider_note: The cause — poor screening by the 4f electrons — is marked as strictly as the definition; an answer that defines the contraction and lists consequences but never says why loses a full mark.
